resistivity.definition: A property of a material that shows how strongly it resists the flow of electric current.

resistor.definition: A component in an electric circuit that opposes the flow of current.

resolution.definition: the ability of an optical instrument to show small details clearly

resolving power.definition: the ability to tell two very close objects apart as separate

retina.definition: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where images are formed.

reversibility of light.definition: the idea that light follows the same path if its direction is reversed

rewirable fuse.definition: A fuse in which the fuse wire can be replaced after it melts.

RGB.definition: A colour system that uses red, green, and blue light to create many colours.

rheostat.definition: A variable resistor used to change the current in a circuit.

right-angle mirror.definition: a pair of mirrors joined so that they make a 90 degree angle

right-hand grip rule.definition: a rule used to find the north pole of a solenoid by curling the fingers of the right hand in the direction of current so the thumb points to the north pole

ring main.definition: a house wiring system in which the cable forms a loop that starts and ends at the consumer unit

rods.definition: special cells in the retina that help us see in dim light

roof prism.definition: a type of prism used in binoculars to turn the image upright in a compact shape

saturation.definition: The state in which a material cannot be magnetised any more because most of its dipoles are already aligned.

scatter.definition: to spread light in many directions

sclera.definition: the tough white outer covering of the eye

secondary cell.definition: a cell that can be recharged after it runs down

secondary colours.definition: colours formed by mixing two primary light colours, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta

secondary image.definition: an image formed after light reflects more than once

secondary rainbow.definition: a fainter rainbow formed outside the primary rainbow by two internal reflections inside raindrops

semiconductor.definition: a material whose ability to conduct electricity is between that of a conductor and an insulator

series.definition: a way of connecting components one after another in a single path

series connection.definition: A way of connecting components end to end so the same current flows through each one.

shadow.definition: a dark area formed when an object blocks light

short circuit.definition: an unwanted connection in a circuit that lets current pass through a very low-resistance path, causing a very large current

short-circuit.definition: an unwanted path in a circuit that lets a very large current flow

shutter.definition: the part of a camera that opens and closes to control how long light enters

sign convention.definition: A set of rules for deciding which distances are positive or negative in calculations.

similar triangles.definition: triangles that have the same shape but may have different sizes

simple microscope.definition: A magnifying device made of one convex lens used to make small objects look bigger.

single-touch method.definition: A method of magnetising using one magnet stroked along a material in one direction.

slide wire bridge.definition: a modified Wheatstone bridge that uses a long wire to find an unknown resistance

Snell’s law.definition: the law stating that for a given pair of materials, the ratio sin(i) to sin(r) stays constant

soft magnetic.definition: Describes a material that is easy to magnetise but loses its magnetism easily.

solar energy.definition: energy that comes from the Sun and can be used to produce electricity or heat

solenoid.definition: a coil of wire wound in loops that produces a magnetic field when electric current flows through it

south pole.definition: The end of a magnet that points south when the magnet is freely suspended.

south-seeking pole.definition: The pole of a magnet that points toward the south when it is free to turn.

spark.definition: a small flash of light produced when electric charge suddenly moves through the air

specimen.definition: a sample or object prepared for study, especially under a microscope

spectrum.definition: the band of colours formed when white light is split

spherical mirror.definition: a curved mirror shaped like part of a sphere

spin.definition: the turning motion of a particle such as an electron around its own axis

stage.definition: the flat part of a microscope where the object or slide is placed

static electricity.definition: electric charge that builds up and stays on the surface of a material instead of flowing as a current

stroking.definition: A method of magnetising in which a magnet is rubbed along a material in one direction many times.

subtended angle.definition: the angle formed by lines drawn from the eye or lens to the top and bottom of an object or image

subtractive colour mixing.definition: A way of making colours by mixing paints, inks, or pigments that absorb some light colours.

subtractive mixing.definition: The mixing of pigments or colours where some light is absorbed, often making darker colours.

sulphated.definition: damaged by too much lead sulphate forming on a battery, so it can no longer recharge properly

surplus.definition: an extra amount more than what is needed or expected

surveillance.definition: careful watching of a place or person, often for safety or security

symmetric.definition: having two halves that match in shape and size

telephoto lens.definition: a lens used to photograph faraway objects so they appear larger

telescope.definition: An instrument used to see distant objects, especially objects in the sky.

temperature.definition: a measure of how hot or cold something is

temperature change.definition: The amount by which temperature increases or decreases.

temporary magnet.definition: A magnet that keeps its magnetism only for a short time or only while a magnetic field is present.

terminal.definition: The end of a cell or component where connection is made.

Tesla.definition: The SI unit used to measure magnetic field strength.

tester.definition: a simple tool used to check whether a wire or socket is live

thermal energy.definition: Heat energy; the energy that makes things warmer.

thermistor.definition: a resistor whose resistance changes with temperature

thin lens.definition: A lens that is treated as very thin, so light is considered to bend at its centre plane.

thin lens formula.definition: The equation 1/f = 1/u + 1/v used to find image position in thin lenses.

three-pin plug.definition: A plug with live, neutral, and earth connections used for safer electrical connection.

thunder.definition: the loud sound caused by the rapid expansion of air heated by lightning

thunderstorm.definition: a storm with lightning, thunder, and often heavy rain and strong winds

tissue.definition: a group of similar cells working together in a living thing

total internal reflection.definition: the complete reflection of light back into a denser material when it tries to move into a less dense material at a large angle

translucent.definition: allowing only some light to pass through, so objects cannot be seen clearly

transmission.definition: the passing of light through a material

transmit.definition: To allow light to pass through something.

transparent.definition: allowing light to pass through so objects can be seen clearly

tree system.definition: a house wiring method where cables branch out from the main supply like branches of a tree

triangular prism.definition: a transparent solid with triangular ends that can bend and split light

triboelectric series.definition: a list of materials arranged by how likely they are to gain or lose electrons when rubbed

two-pin plug.definition: A plug with only two connections, usually live and neutral, and no earth pin.

umbra.definition: the darkest part of a shadow where light is completely blocked

uniform field.definition: A field that has the same strength and direction at every point.

unmagnetised.definition: Not yet made into a magnet.

upright.definition: Describes an image that is in the same vertical position as the object, not turned upside down.

vacuum.definition: a space with no matter, where light travels at its greatest speed

variable capacitor.definition: a capacitor whose capacitance can be changed

variable resistor.definition: a resistor whose resistance can be changed

vertex.definition: the middle point of a curved mirror surface

vertical plane.definition: A flat surface or direction that goes straight up and down.

virtual.definition: In optics, describing a point from which light rays only appear to come.

virtual image.definition: An image that appears to come from a place, but light rays do not actually meet there.

vitreous humour.definition: the clear jelly inside the eye behind the lens that helps keep the eye’s shape

volt.definition: the unit used to measure potential difference

voltage drop.definition: the decrease in electrical potential across a part of a circuit

voltmeter.definition: An instrument used to measure potential difference or voltage.

watt.definition: The SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second.

wavelength.definition: the distance between one wave and the next wave of the same kind

Wheatstone bridge.definition: an electrical circuit used to measure an unknown resistance very accurately

wide angle lens.definition: a lens that captures a wide area in one picture

zoom lens.definition: a lens whose focal length can be changed to make objects look nearer or farther
